title: Bridge Week: All-team alignment + OKR redraft (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft for the Bridge Week cross-company alignment session and an initial redraft of company-level OKRs going into Q2 planning. Goal is to produce a slim, prioritized OKR set + an all-hands-friendly narrative and clear asks for each org.

Context / Why Bridge Week: quick summary:
- We’re mid-cycle and several teams have diverged on scope (Optimize vs Dedicated vs Hosting).
- Need a short, synchronous reset so product and eng can converge on 8–10 execution priorities that map cleanly to exec asks and headcount plans.
- Bridge Week = focused 3-day working sprint (mix of pre-read, alignment sessions, and team syncs) to produce the OKR redraft, a product rollout calendar, and a small decision register.

High-level outcomes we want from the week (deliverables):
1) Company OKR redraft (3 objectives + 2–4 KRs each) in final draft for Exec review by EOW.
2) All-hands run-of-show and 10-min exec update script.
3) Decision register with owners and deadlines (top-10 operational decisions).
4) Resource gap map (hiring/infra-cost asks) to feed Finance for the next budget checkpoint.

Proposed company-level OKRs (first pass, rough metrics):
Objective A: Make inference predictable and cheaper for customers across hosted and private deployments.
- KR A1: Reduce 95th percentile token latency for hosted API by 12% on average across top-5 models (baseline = Dec 2024).
- KR A2: Deliver 2 model-quantization recipes recommended by Redwood Optimize for high-throughput workloads and validate cost savings on 3 customer benchmarks (>=20% token cost reduction).
- KR A3: Increase Redwood Dedicated committed capacity adoption: +25% new reserved contracts YoY (measured in GPU-weeks).

Objective B: Reduce customer-impacting reliability events and improve graceful degradation.
- KR B1: Reduce production incidents causing >5% request loss by 40% quarter-over-quarter.
- KR B2: Implement regional fallback for hosted API and run 2 live failover drills with simulated capacity loss.
- KR B3: Ship per-route SLA reporting in Console (beta) for top 20 customers.

Objective C: Accelerate developer velocity for integrating LLM features.
- KR C1: Ship SDK v3 with streaming and structured outputs that reduces average integration time by 30% (developer survey).
- KR C2: Publish 6 workload playbooks (embedding, reranking, chat, caching, batching, quantization) with reference configs and perf numbers.
- KR C3: Launch a self-serve canary rollout feature in Console and get 10 customers in closed beta.

Notes on measurement:
- Each KR needs a precise owner (team + named lead), a baseline (date + metric), and an automated dashboard link.
- Where we lack instrumentation, put a low-cost telemetry spike during Bridge Week to enable measurement.

Draft all-hands / Bridge Week agenda (3 days) — working format:
Pre-work (to-do before day 1):
- Product teams to submit 1-slide summary of top 3 ship goals (due 48h pre-week).
- Eng leads submit incident postmortem highlights and capacity constraints (short doc).
- Finance to prepare rough cost delta sheet for proposed hires and infra changes.

Day 1 — Alignment & exec framing (remote + in-person hubs)
- 09:00–09:30: Opening (CEO) — Why these next 90 days matter.
- 09:30–11:00: Exec lightning updates (10m each) — state, top open decisions.
- 11:15–12:30: Cross-org surface: current blockers & unresolved tradeoffs (facilitated).
- Afternoon: Breakouts by objective to draft KRs.

Day 2 — KR drafting, decision register, resourcing
- Morning: Breakouts continue — teams produce KR wording + owners + measurement plan.
- Midday: Finance sync — quick pass on cost feasibility.
- Afternoon: Ops & SRE propose 5 reliability guardrails and measure plan.

Day 3 — Finalize, practice all-hands, and delegation
- Morning: Consolidation session — align wording and remove overlaps.
- Midday: Exec rehearsal for town hall + Q&A prep.
- Afternoon: Publish deliverables to Confluence and send exec review packet.

Decision register (top candidates to track):
- DR-1: Do we prioritize low-latency kernel investments vs model-parallel capacity for Q2? Owner: CTO (Evan Brooks) — decision by 2025-01-30.
- DR-2: Enable auto-quantize-by-default in Redwood Optimize for eligible traffic? Owner: Applied ML (Samira Patel) — decision by 2025-02-05.
- DR-3: Turn on regional fallback for EU customers during peak hours (pilot). Owner: Platform Eng (Diego Morales) — decision by 2025-02-07.

Risks & mitigations (quick list):
- Risk: KR measurement gaps (no dashboard for some KRs). Mitigation: allocate 2 engineer-days during Bridge Week to instrument dashboards and add telemetry flags.
- Risk: Overambitious scope leading to >60% of KRs un-actionable. Mitigation: force each objective to max 4 KRs and require tradeoff note.
- Risk: Exec misalignment on hires. Mitigation: create 'must-hire' vs 'nice-to-have' column and get finance sign-off before final OKRs.

Asks for teams (prior to Bridge Week):
- Product: 1-slide top priorities + 1 prioritized dependency list (Jira keys).
- Engineering: short incident abstracts (<1 page) and capacity hotspots (which services are gated by GPU weeks).
- SRE/Platform: short runbook for regional fallback and a cost estimate for running the pilot.
- Growth/CS: 3 customer stories that would benefit from lower latency / cheaper tokens (for all-hands examples).

Open questions / friction points to resolve during the week:
- How do we reconcile Optimize recommendations that reduce cost but increase tail latency for some workloads?
- What is the threshold for gating auto-quantization on customer workloads (safety, accuracy checks)?
- For Dedicated capacity growth targets, what is the minimum commit that triggers enterprise sales involvement?

Communication plan for after Bridge Week:
- Publish final OKR doc + short explainer (one-pager) to Confluence and share in #company-all.
- Execs to run a 10-minute town hall summary and leave 20 minutes for Q&A.
- Team-level goals to be synced in the weekly standups and tracked in the OKR tracker sheet.

Appendix: quick owner mapping (first-pass)
- Objective A owner: Product + Serve (Priya Shah)
- Objective B owner: SRE + Platform (Diego Morales)
- Objective C owner: DevEx + SDK (Marta Nguyen)
- Cross-cutting measurement lead: Analytics (Evan Brooks)

Quick notes / style guidance for KR wording (to use in breakouts):
- Use measurable phrasing (percent, absolute numbers, count, response time).
- Include baseline and target date.
- Prefer customer-impact language ("reduce customer token-cost by X") where possible.

Notes to self / next steps (working):
- Circulate this draft to execs + People Ops for cadence conflicts (Avery).
- Build a simple Confluence template for the deliverables so reviewers have a consistent view.
- Confirm Bridge Week room allocation and remote hub links.

---
Working draft. Expect many edits. Please add concrete KR baselines into the shared sheet (linked above) and comment inline in Confluence draft.
